detection.rule: rear_end / lane_change: event while TTC <= 1.5 s for >= 0.3 s; crossing: PET <= 5.0 s over the shared swept-footprint zone
detection.citation: FHWA SSAM default (Gettman et al. 2008, FHWA-HRT-08-051; SSAM User Manual FHWA-HRT-08-050)

severity_ttc.rule: TTC_min <= 0.5 s critical; 0.5 < TTC_min <= 1.0 s serious; 1.0 < TTC_min <= 1.5 s moderate
severity_ttc.note: study-specific bins within the SSAM TTC <= 1.5 s detection range

severity_pet.rule: PET <= 1 s critical; 1 < PET <= 2.5 s serious; 2.5 < PET <= 5 s moderate
severity_pet.note: study-specific bins (no FHWA/SSAM standard for PET severity)

drac.rule: drac_flag = DRAC_max >= 3.4 m/s^2 (11.2 ft/s^2); reported alongside TTC events, not a detection criterion
drac.citation: AASHTO (2018) A Policy on Geometric Design of Highways and Streets, 7th ed.

ttc.rule: TTC = gap / (v_f - v_l) when v_f > v_l; gap = front-to-rear spacing (m); follower speed >= 2 m/s, gap >= 1 m, closing rate consistent with spacing change

pet.rule: footprint = length x width rectangle behind the front-bumper point, heading from velocity; conflict zone = intersection of the two swept footprints (0.5 m raster, 50 Hz); PET = t(second vehicle front enters zone) - t(first vehicle rear leaves zone); crossing only for conflicting approaches with conflict angle >= 30 deg
pet.citation: Allen et al. (1978) TRR 667; FHWA SSAM (Gettman et al. 2008)

overlap.rule: both footprints inside the shared zone at the same time -> recorded with pet = 0 and overlap = true
overlap.note: a physical overlap at NGSIM position accuracy is most likely a data error (Punzo et al. 2011), not an observed near-collision

pedestrian_pet.rule: pedestrian footprint 0.5 x 0.5 m swept along its track while inside a crosswalk polygon; vehicle footprint as for crossing PET; zone = intersection of the two swept footprints; PET = t(second enters) - t(first leaves); detected at PET <= 5.0 s, any conflict angle; overlap (simultaneous occupancy) recorded with pet = 0
pedestrian_pet.note: study-specific severity bins (PET <= 1 s critical, <= 2 s serious, <= 5 s moderate); video-based VRU studies place conflict thresholds at 1-3 s (Zangenehpour et al. 2016); no FHWA/SSAM standard
pedestrian_pet.citation: Allen et al. (1978) TRR 667; Zangenehpour et al. (2016) AAP 86

failure_to_yield.rule: a vehicle's front enters a crosswalk polygon at t_v while a pedestrian is inside the same polygon, or within 3.0 s before the pedestrian enters it; the vehicle never slowed below 0.5 m/s (1.1 mph) in the 3.0 s before entry; and it had a stopping opportunity: its path distance to the crosswalk when the pedestrian entered (or 3.0 s before its own entry if the pedestrian came second) was at least the AASHTO stopping distance 2.5 s * v + v^2 / (2 * 3.4 m/s^2)
failure_to_yield.severity: study-specific bins: pedestrian already in the crosswalk -> distance from the vehicle's entry point to the pedestrian at entry <= 3.6 m (one lane) critical, <= 7.2 m serious, else moderate; pedestrian arriving after the vehicle -> lead time <= 1 s critical, <= 2 s serious, else moderate
failure_to_yield.note: indicator, not a citation: the roadway-half condition of §552.003(a) and signal phase are not applied; at a signalised site vehicles proceeding on green past a pedestrian crossing against the signal are counted
failure_to_yield.citation: Texas Transportation Code §552.003; Fitzpatrick et al. (2006) NCHRP Report 562 (yielding and opportunity); AASHTO (2018) stopping sight distance

citations: Gettman, D., Pu, L., Sayed, T., Shelby, S. (2008). Surrogate Safety Assessment Model and Validation: Final Report. FHWA-HRT-08-051; SSAM User Manual FHWA-HRT-08-050. Federal Highway Administration.
AASHTO (2018) A Policy on Geometric Design of Highways and Streets, 7th ed.
Allen, B. L., Shin, B. T., Cooper, P. J. (1978). Analysis of traffic conflicts and collisions. Transportation Research Record 667, 67-74.
Texas Transportation Code §552.003 (Pedestrian Right-of-Way at Crosswalk): the operator of a vehicle shall stop and yield the right-of-way to a pedestrian crossing a roadway in a crosswalk.

Fitzpatrick, K., Turner, S., Brewer, M., Carlson, P., Ullman, B., Trout, N., Park, E. S., Whitacre, J., Lalani, N., Lord, D. (2006). Improving Pedestrian Safety at Unsignalized Crossings. TCRP Report 112 / NCHRP Report 562, Transportation Research Board. (Yielding: a driver who stops or slows for the pedestrian; only drivers with stopping distance available count as opportunities.)

Zangenehpour, S., Strauss, J., Miranda-Moreno, L. F., Saunier, N. (2016). Are signalized intersections with cycle tracks safer? A case-control study based on automated surrogate safety analysis using video data. Accident Analysis & Prevention 86, 161-172. (PET thresholds of 1-3 s for vulnerable road user conflicts.)

Punzo, V., Borzacchiello, M. T., Ciuffo, B. (2011). On the assessment of vehicle trajectory data accuracy and application to the Next Generation SIMulation (NGSIM) program data. Transportation Research Part C 19(6), 1243-1262.

sensitivity.note: counts of distinct events at each threshold; TTC events from the same pair series, PET from one footprint pass (min PET per pair)

scatter_note: every TTC event detected at TTC <= 3.0 s; severity null above the 1.5 s detection threshold

yield.note: entries with a pedestrian in the crosswalk (or entering within 3 s); failures are entries that neither stopped nor lacked the stopping distance
